prop:habiro-tail-star-identity:
Proposition Habiro-tail star identity: the 5_2 Masbaum cyclotomic datum equals its bar-inverted q-Borel transform, with the quadratic k-exponent collapsed to linear. Let R be a field and a \in R with a \neq 0. Write \bar q = a^{2} and \tilde q = a^{-2}, let (\,q;q)_n = \prod_{j=1}^{n}(1-q^{j}) denote the q-Pochhammer symbol, let [n,k]_q denote the Gaussian binomial coefficient, and let C_n(a) be the n-th Masbaum cyclotomic coefficient of 5_2. Then for every n \geq 0

C_n(a)\,(\bar q;\bar q)_n^{2}\,a^{-(5n^{2}+7n)}
  \;=\; (-1)^{n}\,(\tilde q;\tilde q)_n^{2}
        \sum_{k=0}^{n} \tilde q^{\,k(n+1)}\,[n,k]_{\tilde q}.

This is the Habiro-tail star identity.

What the identity does

The left-hand side is the Masbaum cyclotomic datum in its native variable a, carrying a quadratic exponent in both n and the summation index k. The right-hand side is a q-Borel transform evaluated at the bar-inverted argument \tilde q, with an exponent that is linear in k. The identity is therefore an exponent-collapse: it trades a quadratic k-dependence for a linear one, and simultaneously exchanges \bar q \leftrightarrow \tilde q.

Two inversion lemmas supply the collapse, one for each factor.

Bar-inversion of the Gaussian binomial. For q \neq 0,

[n,k]_q \;=\; q^{\,k(n-k)}\,[n,k]_{q^{-1}}.

Applied termwise, this converts each summand's a-exponent 3n^{2}+5n+k^{2}-2k-3nk-k(n-k) into 3n^{2}+5n-2k-2nk; the quadratic k^{2} cancels. Multiplying by the overall a^{-(5n^{2}+7n)} leaves -2(n+1)(n+k), that is, exactly (\bar q)^{-n(n+1)}\cdot(\bar q^{-1})^{k(n+1)}.

Bar-inversion of the squared Pochhammer. For q \neq 0,

(\,q;q)_n^{2} \;=\; q^{\,n(n+1)}\,(\,q^{-1};q^{-1})_n^{2}.

This absorbs the residual (\bar q)^{-n(n+1)} prefactor. Squaring is what makes the statement clean: the unsquared inversion carries a sign (-1)^n and the half-exponent n(n+1)/2, and both disappear on squaring.

Consequences

Write \hat T_n(q) = (\,q;q)_n^{2}\sum_{k=0}^{n} q^{k(n+1)}[n,k]_q for the right-hand side up to sign, so that the identity reads C_n(a)(\bar q;\bar q)_n^{2}a^{-(5n^{2}+7n)} = (-1)^n \hat T_n(\tilde q).

Transient structure. The k=0 term of the sum is exactly 1, whence

\hat T_n(q) \;=\; (\,q;q)_n^{2}\Bigl(1 + q^{\,n+1}
  \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} q^{\,k(n+1)}\,[n,k+1]_q\Bigr).

Every correction to the leading (\,q;q)_n^{2} carries a factor q^{n+1}. This is the algebraic source of the transient behaviour observed in the numerical Borel data.

Pochhammer recursion. (\,q;q)_{n+1} = (\,q;q)_n\,(1-q^{\,n+1}), the finite-order step whose limit governs the Borel residue.

The two analytic facts recorded in the computational witnesses — the residue c_\infty = (\tilde q;\tilde q)_\infty^{2} as a convergent infinite product, and the pole ladder at w = -q_0^{\,k} — are limit statements about the archimedean evaluation and are not part of this proposition. What the proposition supplies is their algebraic skeleton: the recursion and the q^{n+1} transient factor of which those limits are taken.

Status

The identity is proved at every order n, over a generic field with no archimedean construct (the statement is pre-wall). It was first established computationally as an exact integer-Laurent equality for n \leq 32 and numerically to 10^{-497} for n \leq 64; the proof discharges that computation for all n.
prop:fivetwo-trace-field:
Proposition The 5_2 saddle cubic has discriminant -23: the invariant trace field is the cubic field of discriminant -23, and its only quadratic is \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23}). Let R be a commutative ring and let y_1, y_2, y_3 \in R satisfy the Vieta relations of the 5_2 saddle cubic,

y_1 + y_2 + y_3 = 2, \qquad
y_1y_2 + y_1y_3 + y_2y_3 = 3, \qquad
y_1y_2y_3 = 1 .

Then their discriminant is

\bigl((y_1 - y_2)(y_1 - y_3)(y_2 - y_3)\bigr)^{2} \;=\; -23 .

Consequently the invariant trace field of the 5_2 knot — the field generated by the shapes of its three ideal tetrahedra — is the cubic field of discriminant -23, K = \mathbb{Q}[\xi] with \xi^{3} - 2\xi^{2} + 3\xi - 1 = 0.

Why the statement is over a generic ring

The discriminant identity is an algebraic consequence of the three symmetric functions and nothing else. It needs no ordering, no square root and no archimedean construct, so it is stated over a generic commutative ring rather than over \mathbb{R} or \mathbb{C}; the geometric reading in the next section is the archimedean specialisation, not the content of the identity.

The proof is Vieta substitution into the symmetric form of the discriminant: 4\cdot 9 - 4\cdot 27 - 4\cdot 8 + 18\cdot 6 - 27 = -23.

The three places, and the shape that is geometric

K has one real embedding and one complex-conjugate pair. Numerically the three roots of \xi^{3} - 2\xi^{2} + 3\xi - 1 are

\xi_{1} \approx 0.78492 + 1.30714\,i, \qquad
\xi_{2} = \bar{\xi_{1}}, \qquad
\xi_{3} \approx 0.43016 ,

and \xi_1 is the geometric solution — the one whose shapes have positive imaginary part and reproduce \mathrm{Vol}(5_2) \approx 2.82812. The reciprocal cubic 1 - 2z + 3z^{2} - z^{3} and the Landen image z^{3} - z^{2} + 1 generate the same field, being related to the above by rational maps; each has discriminant -23.

Among complex cubic fields, -23 is the smallest discriminant in absolute value.

The one quadratic attached to K

K is not Galois. Its Galois closure has group S_3, whose unique index-2 subgroup A_3 fixes exactly one quadratic field, the quadratic resolvent \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{\mathrm{disc}\,K}) = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23}). Since -23 is squarefree this is the whole of it: \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23}) is the only quadratic field attached to the 5_2 trace field.

This matters because the bar involution separates the conjugate pair \xi_1, \bar{\xi_1}, so any bar-odd datum built from the two complex embeddings lands on the \sqrt{-23} line — the structural analogue of the \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) line for the amphichiral 4_1.

What the determinant does not give

\det(5_2) = 7, and the Alexander polynomial \Delta_{5_2}(t) = 2t^{2} - 3t + 2 has discriminant -7 with roots (3 \pm i\sqrt{7})/4. So \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7}) is genuinely attached to 5_2 — as the Alexander root field, equivalently the quadratic subfield of \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7), where the abelian data of the \mathbb{Z}/7 double branched cover lives.

It is not the geometric trace field, and it cannot be a subfield of one: [\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7}):\mathbb{Q}] = 2 does not divide [K:\mathbb{Q}] = 3, so the tower law forbids the embedding outright. The two fields belong to different layers of the knot, and reading the geometric field off the determinant conflates them.
prop:fivetwo-saddle-sum-rule:
Proposition The 5_2 saddle sum rule: the dilogarithm trace over the three tetrahedron shapes closes to -\pi^2/6 - \tfrac12\log^2 t + \tfrac23(\arg a - \pi)^2. There exist a real t and a complex a with

0 < t < 1, \qquad \mathrm{Im}\,a > 0,

both roots of the 5_2 saddle cubic together with \bar a,

t^{3} - 2t^{2} + 3t - 1 = 0, \qquad
a^{3} - 2a^{2} + 3a - 1 = 0, \qquad
\bar a^{3} - 2\bar a^{2} + 3\bar a - 1 = 0,

such that the three extended dilogarithms sum to an explicit elementary expression:

\mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}}(a) + \mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}}(\bar a) + \mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}}(t)
\;=\; -\frac{\pi^{2}}{6} - \frac{(\log t)^{2}}{2} + \frac{2}{3}\bigl(\arg a - \pi\bigr)^{2} .

This is the 5_2 saddle sum rule.

What the statement says

The left-hand side is the dilogarithm potential evaluated at all three tetrahedron shapes of the 5_2 complement at once — the geometric shape a, its complex conjugate, and the real shape t. Summing over the three embeddings of the trace field is a Galois trace, and the assertion is that this trace closes: it equals a combination of \pi^{2}, a squared logarithm, and a squared argument, with no dilogarithm left over.

Three features of the statement separate out.

The right-hand side is real, and manifestly so. Each of its three terms is built from real data — \pi, \log t for t \in (0,1), and \arg a — even though two of the three left-hand summands are individually complex. The imaginary parts of \mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}}(a) and \mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}}(\bar a) cancel against each other, which is the conjugate pair doing exactly what the S_3 structure of the trace field predicts.

The coefficient 2/3 is forced. It descends from the branch relation

2\ell_j - 3m_j = 2\pi i\,\varepsilon_j ,

which the 5_2 gluing equation y^{2} = (1-y)^{3} imposes on the logarithms \ell_j, m_j of the shapes. Contracting that relation across the three embeddings gives \sum_j \ell_j m_j = \tfrac{2}{3}\sum_j \ell_j^{2} - \tfrac{2\pi i}{3}\sum_j \varepsilon_j \ell_j, and the 2/3 in the sum rule is the 2 and the 3 of the gluing exponents. The sum rule is an identity, not a fit, and there is no free constant in it.

The existence quantifier is essential. The statement is \exists\,t,a with the listed properties, and it is proved by exhibiting them — the real root supplies t, and the geometric root supplies a. It is not the assertion that every triple of cubic roots satisfies the identity.

The extended dilogarithm

\mathrm{Li}_2^{\mathrm{ext}} is the corpus's integral continuation of the dilogarithm; it agrees with the principal branch off [1,\infty) and extends across the cut so that the continuation used in the proof stays single-valued along the transport path between the three shapes.

The branch bookkeeping is where the (\arg a - \pi)^{2} term comes from: it records how far the geometric shape's argument has been carried, and it is why the closed form carries an argument-squared rather than only a logarithm-squared. The \varepsilon_j above are the same bookkeeping, in the form the gluing relation sees them.

The proof chain is: the complex five-term identity at (y_3, y_1) and (y_3, y_2); the anharmonic evaluations; the branch equations from y^{2} = (1-y)^{3}; the root data; and the logarithm evaluations. Every step is unconditional, and the existence of the three saddle roots follows from the intermediate value theorem — so the closed form is a statement about the actual roots of X^{3} - 2X^{2} + 3X - 1, rather than about a structure that might be empty.

Why the shape field is \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23}) and not something smaller

The cubic X^3 - 2X^2 + 3X - 1 is irreducible over \mathbb{Q} with discriminant -23, so its splitting field contains the imaginary quadratic subfield \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-23}). Contrast the figure-eight knot, whose shape field is the Eisenstein field \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) and whose tetrahedra are regular. That extra arithmetic is exactly why the 5_2 analysis does not reduce to the 4_1 argument: the 4_1 squeeze rests on positivity of \langle 4_1\rangle_N, which \langle 5_2\rangle_N does not have.

What this does and does not establish

It establishes an exact, parameter-free relation among the three shapes of a chiral hyperbolic knot — the analogue, for 5_2, of the closures available for the amphichiral 4_1.

It is not the volume conjecture. Three statements are distinct and must not be conflated:

  1. the sum rule above, which is proved;
  2. \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus 5_2) = 3\,D(y_1), a statement about a hyperbolic manifold, which is not proved here;
  3. \lim_{N} \frac{2\pi}{N}\log\langle 5_2\rangle_N = \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus 5_2), the volume conjecture for 5_2 — Ohtsuki's theorem [ohtsuki2016], untouched.

The sum rule is an identity among dilogarithm values at algebraic points. Nothing about a metric, a manifold, or an asymptotic follows from it.

It does not by itself supply a bar-odd action value, and no such value is claimed here. The sum rule is symmetric in the conjugate pair: a and \bar a enter identically, so the quantity it pins is bar-even. Extracting a bar-odd datum requires the difference across the conjugate pair, which lands on the \sqrt{-23} line of the trace field and is a separate question from this identity.
rem:fivetwo-bar-odd-arithmetic-home:
Remark The bar-odd channel of 5_2 is confined to the \sqrt{-23} line, and chirality is why the question is asked on 5_2 rather than 4_1. The bar involution q \mapsto q^{-1} acts on the three embeddings of the 5_2 trace field by exchanging the complex-conjugate pair \xi_1 \leftrightarrow \bar{\xi_1} and fixing the real embedding \xi_3. That single observation fixes where a bar-odd datum can live, and it is stated separately from the identity it follows from.

The even and odd channels are geometrically distinguishable

Write P for any quantity attached to an embedding — a shape, a series coefficient, a period. The two combinations

P^{\mathrm{even}} = P(\xi_1) + P(\bar{\xi_1}), \qquad
P^{\mathrm{odd}} = P(\xi_1) - P(\bar{\xi_1})

behave differently under the bar. The even combination is real and is what a Galois trace over the conjugate pair sees; the odd combination is purely imaginary and lies on the \sqrt{-23} axis of K \otimes \mathbb{C}, since \sqrt{-23} generates the quadratic resolvent that A_3 fixes.

The bar-even channel is the one a symmetric pairing can reach; the bar-odd channel is confined to a single line, and that line is determined by the discriminant of the trace field.

Why 5_2 rather than 4_1

For an amphichiral knot the mirror is the knot itself, so the Jones polynomial satisfies J_{K^{*}}(q) = J_K(q^{-1}) = J_K(q) and the bar-odd part vanishes identically. The figure-eight 4_1 is amphichiral; its bar-odd channel is empty for a structural reason.

5_2 is chiral. Its bar-odd channel is not forced to vanish, which is why it is the knot the odd-channel question has to be asked on. The trace-field degree tracks the same distinction: 4_1 has the quadratic \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3}) and 5_2 the cubic of discriminant -23, with a genuine complex-conjugate pair to separate.

What is and is not settled

Settled: the location. Any bar-odd datum assembled from the conjugate pair lies on the \sqrt{-23} line. This is a consequence of the field structure alone and needs no analytic input.

Not settled: the value. Locating the line does not evaluate anything on it, and no bar-odd action value is asserted here or in the propositions this remark interprets. The sum rule (The 5_2 saddle sum rule) is symmetric in the conjugate pair and therefore bar-even; it constrains the even channel and leaves the odd one open.

Alexander layer versus geometric layer

The bar-odd channel's arithmetic home is not \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7}), the field one would infer from \det(5_2) = 7. That is the Alexander layer, not the geometric one, and it cannot be a subfield of a cubic. The line is \sqrt{-23}, already visible in the \sigma-pair data.

The lesson generalises to a question to ask of any such claim: which layer of the knot is this field attached to? Abelian invariants — the determinant, the Alexander polynomial, the branched cover — carry one field; the geometric \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C}) representation carries another. They coincide for no general reason.
prop:fivetwo-dt-spectrum-split:
Proposition The 5_2 DT spectrum \{3,4\} splits across chirality, and no \tau-symmetric scalar can recover the ordered datum. Let \tau denote the chirality involution — the mirror / q \mapsto q^{-1} swap — acting on the ordered pair of leading Stokes constants (\mathrm{dt}^{+}, \mathrm{dt}^{-}) of the 5_2 knot. Then for every \tau-symmetric integer reading g, that is every g with g(a,b) = g(b,a),

g(\mathrm{dt}^{+}, \mathrm{dt}^{-}) = g(\mathrm{dt}^{-}, \mathrm{dt}^{+}),
\qquad\text{while}\qquad
\mathrm{dt}^{+} - \mathrm{dt}^{-} \neq 0 .

Hence no \tau-symmetric scalar recovers the ordered datum.

For 5_2 the leading Stokes matrices are 3 \times 3 and carry

\mathrm{dt}^{+} = S^{+}(0)_{01} = 4, \qquad
\mathrm{dt}^{-} = S^{-}(0)_{02} = 3 ,

so the DT spectrum \{3,4\} is split across chirality: the 4 lives in S^{+}, the 3 in S^{-}, and the bar-odd part of the pair is 1 \neq 0.

Why 4_1 cannot show this

For the figure-eight the Stokes block is 2 \times 2, with q \to 0 form

S^{+}(0) = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix},

carrying the single off-diagonal integer 3. Because 4_1 is amphichiral, S^{+} and S^{-} are related by the amphichiral involution, and the scalar 3 is simultaneously the off-diagonal entry, the symmetry constant, and the whole spectrum. There is nothing to separate.

Chirality is exactly what breaks that degeneracy. For 5_2 the four natural readings of the leading Stokes data are four different integers:

the \tau-even sum \mathrm{dt}^{+} + \mathrm{dt}^{-} = 7, the two spectrum members \mathrm{dt}^{+} = 4 and \mathrm{dt}^{-} = 3, and the \tau-odd difference \mathrm{dt}^{+} - \mathrm{dt}^{-} = 1. These are pairwise distinct, so the amphichiral collapse — all four readings equal, as they are for 4_1 — does not occur.

The 7 here is the \tau-even sum 4+3 and nothing more. It is not identified with \det(5_2) = 7, and no such identification is claimed or implied. The two sevens arise from unrelated constructions; reading one off the other is the conflation that produced a retracted claim elsewhere in this lane.

What the exclusion is worth

The statement is universally quantified over g, so it is a structural exclusion, not a failed search: it is not that no symmetric scalar has been found, but that none can exist. Any construction whose output is symmetric under exchanging the two Stokes blocks is blind to the datum, however elaborate.

The same fact says the DT count is a bar-graded object. The involution \tau induces a faithful \mathbb{Z}/2 grading into bar-even and bar-odd parts; the 5_2 pair has nonzero bar-odd part, and that part is precisely what a symmetric reading discards. "No scalar serves the datum" and "the bar-odd part is nonzero" are the same statement.

Scope

The matrices above are the q \to 0 coefficient matrices, so every assertion here is a finite decidable identity about concrete integer matrices — there is no analysis in it. What is not established is any statement about the full q-series beyond leading order, and no bar-odd action value follows: the grading locates the datum, it does not evaluate it.
prop:fivetwo-stokes-unimodular:
Proposition The leading 5_2 Stokes matrices are unimodular and mutually inverse under transposition, and the W_{-1} block has determinant -2. Let S^{+}(0) and S^{-}(0) be the leading (q \to 0) coefficient matrices of the 5_2 Stokes sandwich, as 3 \times 3 integer matrices. Then

\det S^{+}(0) = \det S^{-}(0) = 1,
\qquad
\bigl(S^{+}(0)\bigr)^{\mathsf{T}} \, S^{-}(0) = I .

Moreover the leading W_{-1} block, which is rational rather than integral, has

\det W_{-1}(0) = -2 .

What the three statements do

Unimodularity. \det S^{\pm}(0) = 1 is the leading-order instance of the \det S^{\pm}(q) = 1 condition that a Stokes sandwich must satisfy. It is the algebraic expression of the fact that Stokes matrices are transition data between asymptotic sectors: they change the basis, they do not change the volume.

The inversion relation. (S^{+})^{\mathsf{T}} S^{-} = I at leading order says the two chirality blocks are not independent — one is determined by the other, transposed. This is the sense in which S^{+} and S^{-} are a sandwich rather than two unrelated matrices, and it holds at each of the first several orders in q, not only at q^{0}.

Note that the inversion relation constrains the pair without collapsing it. Transposition is not the chirality involution: it relates the blocks while leaving the ordered pair of off-diagonal constants genuinely ordered, which is why the split recorded in The 5_2 DT spectrum \{3,4\} splits across chirality survives.

The W_{-1} determinant. The magnitude 2 is the "\det \pm 2" phenomenon of the W_{-1} block. The sign matters and is easy to get wrong: W_{-1}(0) carries denominators of 6 from the c-slot subtraction, so it is a matrix over \mathbb{Q} and its determinant is -2. An earlier framing assumed a fitted integer +2; the honest statement is the rational one.

Why these are finite checks

Every assertion above is a finite decidable identity about a concrete matrix with rational entries. There is no analysis, no limit and no convergence argument — the content is entirely in having the right matrices, which come from the derived sandwich compute rather than from a fit.

That is also the limit of what is claimed. These are statements about the leading coefficient matrices; the corresponding all-orders statements (\det S^{\pm}(q) = 1 as an identity of q-series, and Stokes integrality) are checked numerically in the sandwich compute and are not proved here.
prop:fivetwo-level-seven-ladder:
Proposition The level-seven ladder: three five-term instances give the three \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)^{+} numerators, with the 7 supplied by the quadratic residues mod 7. Let R be a commutative ring, L : R \to R an abstract function, and L_1, w_2, q, r, s \in R. Assume the four reflection relations

L(1-x) = L_1 - L(x)
\qquad\text{for } x \in \{w_2,\, q,\, r,\, s\},

and three instances of the five-term relation, h_A, h_B, h_C. Then the three level-seven numerators follow, and in particular

7\bigl(T_1 + T_2 + T_3\bigr) = 21\,L_1 .

The ladder this discharges

Route 8 transports the 5_2 saddle sum rule to the totally real cyclotomic field \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)^{+}, and Route 9 reduces it to three explicit values

\mathrm{Re}\bigl[2L(w_k) + L(-w_k)\bigr] = m_k\,\frac{\pi^{2}}{42},
\qquad m = (17,\, 5,\, -1),
\qquad w_k = 1 + 2\cos\frac{2\pi k}{7} .

The proposition derives those three numerators from three five-term instances alone. Summing them gives \sum_k \mathrm{Re}[2L(w_k)+L(-w_k)] = \pi^{2}/2 = 3L_1, which is Route 8's target and hence the sum rule.

Where the 7 comes from

The certificate is

7T_1 = h_A - 4h_B + 2h_C, \qquad
7T_2 = 4h_A - 2h_B + h_C, \qquad
7T_3 = 2h_A - h_B + 4h_C .

The three coefficient triples are cyclic shifts of (1,2,4) — the quadratic residues mod 7. That is where the 7 in m_k/7 originates: not from an identity that happens to have a seven in it, but from the multiplicative structure of (\mathbb{Z}/7)^{\times} acting on the three real conjugates.

Why the cleared form, and not the divided one

The statement multiplies through by 7 rather than dividing. The divided form is genuinely unavailable, and for a sharper reason. In characteristic 7 the same hypotheses force 3L_1 = 0, hence L_1 = 0 since 3 is invertible mod 7, and every target degenerates to 0 = 0.

So the cleared form is true everywhere and carries content exactly where 7 is invertible, while the divided form would be vacuous precisely where it could not be stated.

Scope

L is abstract: nothing here depends on a dilogarithm implementation or on the Bloch group, matching the treatment in The 5_2 saddle sum rule where the reflection identity is likewise an explicit hypothesis.

Correspondingly, this derives the numerators given the five-term instances and reflection. It does not prove the five-term relation itself, the inversion/Landen extensions, or Route 8's transport. Those remain inputs.
rem:fivetwo-three-sevens:
Remark Three different sevens attach to 5_2 — the determinant, the \tau-even Stokes sum, and the cyclotomic level — and none of them is the trace field. Three different sevens attach to the 5_2 knot. They arise from unrelated constructions, they live on different layers, and identifying any two of them is unsupported. The corpus has already lost a claim to exactly that error, so the distinctions are recorded explicitly here.

The three

The determinant. \det(5_2) = |\Delta_{5_2}(-1)| = 7, where \Delta_{5_2}(t) = 2t^{2} - 3t + 2 has discriminant -7 and roots (3 \pm i\sqrt{7})/4. This seven is abelian: it belongs to the Alexander polynomial and the \mathbb{Z}/7 double branched cover, and the field it generates is \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7}), the imaginary quadratic subfield of \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7).

The \tau-even Stokes sum. The leading Stokes constants of the two chirality blocks satisfy \mathrm{dt}^{+} + \mathrm{dt}^{-} = 4 + 3 = 7 (The 5_2 DT spectrum \{3,4\} splits across chirality). This seven is a sum of two integers, not a field invariant, and no arithmetic meaning is attached to it; it appears in the corpus only as one of four distinct readings used to show that no single scalar reproduces the leading Stokes data.

The cyclotomic level. The level-seven ladder (The level-seven ladder) lives in \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)^{+}, the totally real cubic subfield generated by w_k = 1 + 2\cos(2\pi k/7), and its seven enters through the quadratic residues \{1,2,4\} mod 7.

None of them is the trace field

The invariant trace field is the cubic of discriminant -23 (The 5_2 saddle cubic has discriminant -23), which is a fourth object again. Two comparisons are inviting, and both fail.

\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-7}) cannot sit inside the trace field: 2 \nmid 3, so the tower law forbids it. That is the exclusion the determinant-to-trace-field reading violates.

\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_7)^{+} has the same degree as the trace field — both are cubic — and their minimal polynomials even open the same way,

x^{3} - 2x^{2} - x + 1
\qquad\text{versus}\qquad
x^{3} - 2x^{2} + 3x - 1 .

They are nevertheless different fields, and not marginally: the first has discriminant 49, is totally real and cyclic; the second has discriminant -23, is non-Galois with Galois group S_3, and has one real place and a complex-conjugate pair. Matching degrees and matching leading coefficients are not evidence of anything.

The reusable form

Before attaching a field to a knot invariant, ask which layer the invariant belongs to. Abelian data — the determinant, the Alexander polynomial, the branched cover — carries one field. The geometric \mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C}) representation carries another. A cyclotomic level appearing in a transported identity carries a third. They coincide for no general reason, and a shared numeral is not a shared structure.
prop:fivetwo-envelope-transport:
Proposition The 5_2 envelope transports to S(\pi) - S(0) = \pi^2, tolerating the one point where the root labelling fails. Let S(\varphi) = \sum_j \mathrm{Re}\, V(x(\varphi), y_j(\varphi)) be the envelope of the 5_2 deformed saddle along the unit-circle arc x(\varphi) = e^{i\varphi}. Suppose S is continuous on [0,\pi] and satisfies

\frac{dS}{d\varphi} = 2\varphi
\qquad\text{for every } \varphi \in [0,\pi) \text{ except possibly one point.}

Then

S(\pi) - S(0) = \pi^{2} .

The one exceptional point is not a fudge

The excluded point is \varphi_0, where the discriminant of the saddle curve vanishes. There two root branches collide, and no differentiable labelling of the three roots exists through it. That is a genuine monodromy obstruction, not a gap in the argument, and the honest response is the one taken here: the three root-paths y_1, y_2, y_3 enter as parameters, and their differentiability is a hypothesis rather than a construction.

What makes this harmless is that S is a symmetric function of the roots. As a function of \varphi it therefore needs no labelling at all — it is well defined and continuous across \varphi_0, precisely where the individual branches collide and swap. The labelling is required only to differentiate term by term, which is a local operation, so it is needed only away from \varphi_0.

In general, a symmetric function of a family of roots is insensitive to the monodromy that permutes them, and an obstruction to labelling the branches is not an obstruction to the symmetric total.

Non-vacuity is proved, not assumed

A conditional statement is worthless if its hypotheses are unsatisfiable, and that is checked here: a companion result exhibits S(\varphi) = \varphi^{2} satisfying both hypotheses, with the conclusion reading \pi^{2} = 0 + \pi^{2}.

That example is deliberately trivial — its purpose is to rule out the vacuous reading, not to supply evidence. The check with real content is numerical: on the actual arc, S' = 2\varphi holds per root to 4.6 \times 10^{-41} and summed to 9.2 \times 10^{-41}.

Scope

The derivative hypothesis is an input. What is proved here is the passage from that hypothesis to the total \pi^{2}, tolerating one exceptional point — the integration step, not the identification of the integrand. The numerical measurement above is what supports the integrand; the integrand itself is not proved.
prop:fivetwo-discriminant-vanishes:
Proposition The GGM curve's discriminant vanishes on the unit circle — two root branches do collide on the arc. The discriminant of the GGM curve vanishes somewhere on the unit circle:

\exists\, x \in \mathbb{C}, \quad \|x\| = 1 \ \text{ and } \ \mathrm{disc}(x) = 0 .

So two of the three root branches collide on the arc.

What this refutes

The transport argument had recorded a sub-gap as closed on the grounds that

the three branches y_j(x) are continuous and never collide on the arc (\min|\mathrm{disc}| = 0.348), so g is continuous,

and stated the envelope theorem's implicit-function hypothesis as satisfied on the same constant. Both are false.

The 0.348 was a grid minimum from an \approx 360-point scan of [0,\pi]. The dip is narrow — |\mathrm{disc}'| \approx 87 near the zero — so refining the scan gives 0.068, then 0.0068, then 0. A minimum over samples is a bound on the samples, not on the function.

Why the refutation is short

It needs no analysis of the branches at all. Three ingredients:

The discriminant is palindromic. Hence \mathrm{disc}(x) = x^{4}\,Q(x + 1/x) with

Q(u) = u^{4} - 6u^{3} + 7u^{2} + 6u - 31 ,

a field_simp; ring identity.

Q changes sign on (-2,-1). Q(-2) = 49 > 0 > -23 = Q(-1), so the intermediate value theorem gives a real root there. (It sits at u \approx -1.4844.)

(-2,-1) is reachable. The points of \|x\| = 1 are exactly those with x + 1/x real in [-2,2], which contains (-2,-1).

So the whole argument is polynomial algebra plus one application of the IVT, and the two evaluations are exact rational arithmetic.

The conclusion survives; only the argument dies

This refutes the reasoning, not the transport's result. S sums over all roots and is therefore symmetric, and a collision merely permutes the roots — a symmetric function cannot notice a permutation. Numerically, S(e^{i\varphi}) - S(1) = \varphi^{2} holds to 4 \times 10^{-40} through the branch point.

What dies is the per-root labelling, and only the argument used labels. This is why the envelope statement (The 5_2 envelope transports to S(\pi) - S(0) = \pi^2) is phrased to tolerate exactly one exceptional point: that point is this collision.

Two appearances of -23, one meaningful and one not

At x = 1 the curve degenerates to the saddle cubic y^{3} - 2y^{2} + 3y - 1, so \mathrm{disc}(1) = -23 is the trace-field discriminant (The 5_2 saddle cubic has discriminant -23) — the same object, recovered at the base point.

Q(-1) = -23 as well, and that one is a coincidence: Q takes the value -23 at u = -1, u = 1 and u = 2 alike, and only u = 2 corresponds to x = 1. Nothing is claimed from the other two.
prose:sm-intro:
Scope and epistemic status.

The Standard Model organises the observable interactions around the gauge group \mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1) acting on point-like fields. The present framework is built instead on extended objects — knots, braids, and topological states — whose natural symmetries are not group actions on points but categorical: the gauge transformations are the reversible deformations, braiding operations, and cobordism moves connecting one topological state to another, and these organise into a groupoid rather than a group. This appendix assembles the framework's route from that categorical gauge symmetry to the Standard Model gauge sector.

The route has four stages. First, the gauge symmetry itself is defined as an action groupoid: a groupoid of topological states equipped with an action functional, additive under composition, that records the cost mandated by the categorical Lagrangian (Section on the categorical gauge symmetry). Second, this symmetry is conjectured to realise faithfully inside the Hecke algebra H_n(q), so that the algebraic engine of the derivation chain and the gauge structure are two presentations of the same object (Hecke realization). Third, the archimedean truncation of the gauge symmetry — its image at observable scales under the fibre functor \tau — is conjectured to contain \mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1) (Archimedean truncation). Fourth, the action functional acts as a selection rule, and the conservation laws of the Standard Model appear as invariants constant on gauge orbits.

Calibration convention. Wherever this appendix requires a dimensional scale, it uses the ideal mathematical calibration triple of the framework: the leptonic mass scale m_e (the dimensional unit), the neutron \beta-sector bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} (whose numerical proxy m_\mu/m_e \approx \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 pins the aether modulus q_0), and the pion-sector bar-even channel P_{\mathrm{avg}}^{\pi} (proxy m_\pi). The proton-anchor precision substitution belongs to the physical-observations layer and is not adopted here; it is referenced only where a precision statement must quote the \mu–p aether tension. All scale-bearing statements in the parameter sections below are to be read against this triple.

The epistemic status of each stage is stated where it appears, and the appendix closes with a consolidated ledger of open problems (Open problems). The tiers used are: proved (with complete proof), derived (obtained from framework structure without fitted parameters, machine-verified numerically), conjectural (stated precisely as a hypothesis, with no proof), and open (a precisely identified missing object). In particular: the groupoid formalism and its basic lemmas are proved; the fibre gauge group \mathrm{SU}(2) is an established theorem of the framework; the Coulomb charge Q = w/2 and the writhe-to-isospin map are derived; the Hecke realization, the Standard-Model truncation, and the electroweak torus-link identifications are conjectural; the hypercharge assignment and the \mathrm{SU}(3) colour factor are open. No stage of this appendix is a derivation of the Standard Model; the appendix records how far the derivation currently reaches and exactly what is missing.
def:gauge-action-groupoid:
Definition Gauge action groupoid. Let R be an additive abelian group of action values. A gauge action groupoid over R is a groupoid \mathbf{G} — objects the topological states (knot and braid configurations), morphisms the gauge transformations (reversible deformations, braiding operations, cobordism moves) — equipped with an action functional

  \mathrm{act} \colon \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{G}}(X, Y) \to R

satisfying, for all states X, Y, Z and composable gauge transformations f \colon X \to Y and g \colon Y \to Z,

  \mathrm{act}(\mathrm{id}_X) = 0,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{act}(g \circ f) = \mathrm{act}(f) + \mathrm{act}(g).

Two states X, Y are gauge equivalent when \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{G}}(X, Y) \neq \emptyset.
rem:sm-lagrangian-selection-rules:
Remark The action functional as selection rule. Three consequences of the gauge-action-groupoid structure of the definition are proved, and each carries a physical reading.

Reversal refunds the action. For every gauge transformation f, \mathrm{act}(f^{-1}) = -\mathrm{act}(f): a closed gauge loop costs zero action. This is the statement that gauge transformations are symmetries, not processes — the action functional distinguishes deformations only up to gauge orbit.

Gauge equivalence is an equivalence relation. A physical process connecting an initial to a final topological state is allowed exactly when a gauge transformation connects them. Selection rules are therefore reachability statements in \mathbf{G}: a decay is forbidden when the initial and final states lie in distinct gauge orbits. Conserved quantities are functions on states constant on gauge orbits. The framework currently exhibits two such invariants without fitted parameters: the Coulomb charge Q = w/2 of the Coulomb-charge definition (with w the writhe), which is not the electric charge, and the writhe-to-isospin assignment w \mapsto I_3, which matches sign and ratio across the nucleon doublet scale-free when w is the writhe of the inter-nucleon arc (the ruled nucleon word itself has writhe 0 for both nucleons). Both are constant on the horizontal (conjugation, fixed strand number) orbits only, and are evaluated at the tower's lowest level. This restriction is not optional: conjugation preserves the writhe, whereas the vertical move \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1} shifts the writhe by \pm 1 while presenting the same link, so Q shifts by \pm 1/2 there. Since the brane-tower gauge structure counts the vertical move as part of the gauge freedom, a writhe-derived quantity is a function of the state only once a level is fixed. States are Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms, and the observable is the trace at the minimal level — the braid index, itself a link invariant — so the choice of level is canonical rather than arbitrary. The hypercharge Y is not among them; the writhe map is falsified as a hypercharge assignment, and the missing object is a second, independent crossing invariant.

Residual symmetries form a monoid. The zero-action automorphisms of a fixed state are closed under composition — the unbroken symmetries of that state. The broken part of the symmetry is graded by the action cost.

Two cautions bound this interpretation. First, the suppression of high-action morphisms at observable scales — the mechanism by which the full categorical symmetry would reduce to an effective low-energy group — is a heuristic; no derivation of a suppression rate exists in the framework, and the remark on self-duality as constrained 2-group gauge theory records the higher-categorical refinement (morphisms between morphisms) that the present groupoid formalism truncates away. Second, transition amplitudes of gauge morphisms do not constitute an independent mass mechanism: the framework's masses derive from the volume–density and muon-anchored Hecke-energy chain, and any amplitude-based reading of mass hierarchies must reduce to that chain rather than compete with it. Neither caution is discharged in this appendix; both appear in the closing ledger.

The action functional of the gauge action groupoid is the datum through which the categorical Lagrangian governs the gauge symmetry: \mathrm{act}(f) records the action cost mandated by the categorical action for executing the deformation f. Reversibility of gauge transformations is exactly the groupoid axiom; the base ring R stays generic, with the archimedean specialisation R = \mathbb{R} deferred to the observable side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.
conj:gauge-hecke-realization:
Conjecture Hecke realization of the gauge symmetry. The conjecture is that the gauge symmetry of the knot-state groupoid realises faithfully inside the Hecke algebra: for every topological state X, there is an injective monoid homomorphism

  \Phi_X \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{G}}(X) \longrightarrow H_n(q)

from the gauge automorphisms of X into the multiplicative monoid of H_n(q).

The surjective part of this picture is standard and is not the conjectural content: the braid group B_n maps onto H_n(q) by imposing the Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 on the braid generators, as recorded in the Hecke-algebra-from-braiding remark. The conjectural content is faithfulness on gauge automorphisms: the Hecke relation is a quotient, and a quotient can collapse symmetry. The conjecture asserts that no gauge transformation of a physical state is collapsed — gauge equivalence computed in the Hecke image coincides with gauge equivalence computed in \mathbf{G}, so that the Markov-trace evaluation of the derivation chain sees the full gauge structure rather than a proper quotient of it.

Consequences, contingent on the conjecture: gauge invariance of an observable becomes equivalent to topological invariance of the corresponding Hecke class, and the generators of the gauge symmetry acquire the concrete matrix realisations (Hoefsmit) already used by the compute layer. Neither consequence is available unconditionally.

Read through the canonical quotient, with the gauge automorphisms of an n-strand state identified with B_n, the conjecture is the faithfulness of the Iwahori--Hecke representation B_n \to H_n(q)^{\times}. Its status in the literature is sharp. The reduced Burau representation is a summand of H_n(q), so Burau faithfulness gives Hecke faithfulness at generic q: this covers n = 3 (Magnus--Peluso) and n = 4 (Bharathram--Birman--Brendle, a 2026 preprint, arXiv:2607.05283). Burau is unfaithful for n \geq 5, and whether the full Hecke representation of B_n is faithful for n \geq 5 is an open problem; for those n the conjecture contains it. The Lawrence--Krammer representation, faithful for all n [bigelow2001], does not support the conjecture: it factors through the Birman--Murakami--Wenzl algebra, not through H_n(q). The case n = 2 is proved exactly: on B_2 \cong \mathbb{Z} the quotient is injective if and only if q is not a root of unity (braidTwo_hecke_injective_iff in QOU/StandardModel/GaugeHeckeCanonicalFaithfulness.lean). Two residues remain open. Faithfulness at generic q does not imply faithfulness at a specialised value; for B_3 the faithful real specialisations of Burau are classified only partially. And the gauge automorphism monoids of the state groupoid must first be identified with braid groups. The Lean class GaugeHeckeRealization asks only for some injective homomorphism into H, which is weaker than the canonical reading stated here; the canonical reading is FaithfulVia in the same module.
conj:sm-gauge-truncation:
Conjecture Standard-Model truncation: \mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1) in the archimedean gauge image. The conjecture is that the archimedean truncation of the categorical gauge symmetry — the image of the gauge action groupoid's symmetries at observable scales under the fibre functor \tau — contains the Standard Model gauge group: there is a group G_{\mathrm{arch}} receiving the truncation together with an injective group homomorphism

  \mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1)
  \;\hookrightarrow\;
  G_{\mathrm{arch}}.

The statement is deliberately containment, not isomorphism: the truncation may carry symmetry beyond the Standard Model factors, and the global form of the physical gauge group is (\mathrm{SU}(3) \times \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{U}(1))/\Gamma with \Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{Z}_6 undetermined by current experiment [tong2017]; an isomorphism claim would overstate both what the framework supports and what experiment fixes. A completed derivation would, conversely, have to predict \Gamma — a sharper falsifiable output than the containment itself.

The per-factor evidence is uneven, and the conjecture must be read against a structural constraint the framework has already proved. By the \mathrm{SU}(2)-emergence theorem, the gauge group of tensor automorphisms of a single quantum observable universe fibre is exactly \mathrm{SU}(2) (or its split real form). Consequently the embedding above cannot land in the gauge group of one fibre: any realisation of the \mathrm{SU}(3) and \mathrm{U}(1) factors must come from symmetry visible only at the groupoid level — multi-strand structure, framing data, and the interaction of distinct fibres — and a proposed realisation that places all three factors inside \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) of one fibre contradicts a proved theorem of the framework.

Current per-factor status. The \mathrm{SU}(2) factor is the proved fibre gauge group. For the \mathrm{U}(1) factor, the framing phase supplies a derived charge — the Coulomb charge Q = w/2 of the Coulomb-charge definition, evaluated at the tower's lowest level, since the writhe is preserved by conjugation but shifted by \pm 1 under stabilisation; this charge is not the electric charge, because the proton and neutron share the ruled nucleon word, of writhe 0 — and the writhe ladder of the inter-nucleon arc matches the third isospin component I_3 across the nucleon doublet without a fitted scale (a comparison made at fixed strand number, so the level caveat does not weaken it); the hypercharge Y, however, is not obtained: the writhe map is falsified as a Y assignment (the proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their writhes differ), and the precisely identified missing object is a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe. One candidate direction, recorded here without endorsement, is the ribbon-framing twist: on a framed link the twist and the writhe are exactly the two independent components of the self-linking number, and the helon model of Bilson-Thompson reads electric charge off ribbon twist in units of e/3 [bilson-thompson2005]; whether a per-strand framing datum exists categorically in this framework, and whether it survives the Gell-Mann–Nishijima and hypercharge-spectrum consistency batteries, is untested. For the \mathrm{SU}(3) factor no categorical derivation exists; what is available here is octonion and colour-complex-structure fragments consistent with a colour sector, but no construction of an \mathrm{SU}(3) action from the three-strand structure. The electroweak isotypic decomposition proposed in the G-action-on-aether conjecture and the torus-link identifications of the electroweak triplet conjecture are themselves conjectural inputs, not support.

Finally, the truncation mechanism — the suppression of high-action morphisms at observable scales that would reduce the full categorical symmetry to an effective finite-dimensional group — is a heuristic with no derivation. The conjecture as stated therefore asserts only the containment; it does not assert that the containment is induced by any particular freeze-out mechanism.
conj:sm-hypercharge-invariant:
Conjecture The hypercharge invariant. The conjecture is that the knot-state groupoid carries a hypercharge invariant: functions I_3, Y on states, constant on gauge orbits, satisfying the Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation

  Q \;=\; I_3 + \tfrac{1}{2}\,Y

against the derived charge Q of the Coulomb-charge definition, such that Y does not factor through the writhe w.

The non-factorization clause is the sharp content, and it is not an arbitrary stipulation: the proton and neutron share Y = +1 while their inter-nucleon arc writhes differ, so any writhe function fails on the nucleon doublet, which falsifies the writhe as a hypercharge assignment. Two facts are proved: the factorization criterion — Y factors through w exactly when Y is constant on writhe fibres — and, as a consequence, that any hypercharge invariant forces a writhe-degenerate pair of states separated by Y. The conjecture therefore asserts precisely that the state space carries one more independent \mathrm{U}(1)'s worth of gauge-invariant data than the writhe provides.

One candidate for the second datum is recorded without endorsement in the truncation conjecture: the ribbon-framing twist. The helon model [bilson-thompson2005] is precedent for a twist that encodes electric charge, not hypercharge: in that model the weak hypercharges are put in by hand, and matching a twist invariant to hypercharge is left open. The rotation (Whitney degree) r of a knot diagram is a second published crossing-diagram invariant independent of the writhe, used with w to assign charge labels in the \mathrm{SL}_q(2) knot model [finkelstein2008, §2]; it is recorded here as a candidate on the same terms, without endorsement. Any candidate must pass two batteries before being wired anywhere: the Gell-Mann–Nishijima consistency against the derived Q and I_3 on the nucleon doublet, and the first-generation hypercharge spectrum with its \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility relations [baez-huerta2010], whose global form also arises geometrically as the intersection S(\mathrm{U}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(3)) of maximal-rank subgroups of F_4 [todorov2018]. A candidate that requires tuning a coupling to pass either battery is a fit, not a derivation, and does not instantiate this class.
def:strand-twist-datum:
Definition Per-strand framing (twist) datum. Let \beta be an n-strand state of the gauge-action groupoid. A per-strand framing datum on \beta is a function

  t \colon \{1, \dots, n\} \longrightarrow \mathbb{Z},

assigning to each strand an integer ribbon twist, together with the total twist T(t) = \sum_i t_i. The pair (\beta, t) is a framed state. The datum is an independent label on \beta, not the twist the ambient ribbon structure already carries.
rem:strand-twist-datum-remark:
Remark Properties of the per-strand framing datum and the hypercharge candidate. The per-strand framing datum is not a reading of the ribbon structure. In a ribbon category the twist \theta is determined by the braiding rather than freely assigned, and on the n-th Jones–Wenzl idempotent e_n it acts by the scalar (-1)^n A^{n(n+2)} [habiro2000], whose exponent is the Casimir n(n+2) of the colour. A ribbon twist therefore admits no free per-strand integer, and t is an addition to the structure, not a reading of it.

Three properties of the per-strand framing datum are proved. The residual S_n strand-relabelling action of the gauge groupoid preserves both T(t) and the full multiset \{t_1, \dots, t_n\}, so the datum descends to the horizontal (S_n, fixed-n) orbits. It is not yet known to descend to the vertical direction: stabilisation \beta \in B_n \mapsto \beta\sigma_n^{\pm 1} \in B_{n+1} adds a strand, hence a new entry t_{n+1}, and generically changes both the multiset and T(t). Since the writhe fails at exactly this move (proved in the Lean library), and the point of this datum is to supply what the writhe cannot, the vertical behaviour is the property most worth establishing — it is untested here. As with Q and I_3, the working convention evaluates the datum on the canonical Gröbner–Shirshov word at the tower's minimal level, where only the horizontal action survives. The bar involution (orientation reversal, the conjugate state) negates the datum, T(\bar t) = -T(t), so conjugate states carry opposite twist. Finally, T separates states at fixed writhe: over any fixed braid word — hence any fixed w — there exist framings with distinct total twist. The hypercharge conjecture requires exactly such a coordinate, since its factorization criterion shows any hypercharge invariant must separate a writhe-degenerate pair and no function of w can. The separation is a property of the free label. It is not a property of the ambient ribbon twist, which is constant on a fixed object by the paragraph above, so a candidate resting on it inherits the freedom of the label rather than the rigidity of the category. Supplying a separating coordinate is a necessary condition on the candidate, not evidence that the separation is physical.

The normalised candidate pairs the datum with the derived isospin: with Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = T(t)/3 (the colour-tube charge quantum of the quark picture, the helon-model normalisation [bilson-thompson2005], where the twist encodes the electric charge and the hypercharge is not encoded; the braided-ribbon-graph successor identifies twist with a U(1) charge conserved under the evolution moves [bilsonthompson2007, §V]) and I_3 the writhe-derived isospin, the candidate hypercharge is Y_t = 2\,(Q_{\mathrm{twist}} - I_3). This makes the Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation hold by construction if and only if the two independent charge routes agree, Q_{\mathrm{twist}} = Q against the crossing-derived Coulomb charge — a falsifiable consistency between framing and crossing data, not a definition. That consistency, together with the first-generation spectrum and its \mathbb{Z}_6 compatibility [baez-huerta2010], is the battery any candidate must pass before wiring; it is exactly the open content of the hypercharge conjecture, and no numerical claim is made here.
conj:sm-colour-stabilizer-action:
Conjecture Colour stabilizer action on the state space. The conjecture is that the colour algebra acts faithfully and linearly on the framework's state space: writing \mathfrak{g} for the colour algebra — the intended realisation is the stabilizer \mathfrak{su}(3) = \ker(\mathrm{ev}_e) \subset \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) of a unit imaginary octonion, the Günaydin–Gürsey colour subalgebra, carried here with the proved gate \dim \mathfrak{su}(3) = 8 \iff \mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{ev}_e) = 6 — there is an injective \mathbb{Q}-linear map

  \Phi \colon \mathfrak{g} \longrightarrow \mathrm{End}(V)

into the endomorphisms of the three-strand state space V. This is the missing \mathrm{SU}(3) ingredient of the truncation conjecture at the infinitesimal level: the colour algebra is constructed here [baez2002] [dubois-violette2016], and its realisation as the subgroup of G_2 fixing the octonionic unit e_7, acting on the minimal left ideals of \mathbb{C}\otimes\mathbb{O}, is the construction of [furey2016, §6.2], but no construction makes it act on the states. Bracket compatibility is the natural strengthening, deliberately omitted from the class so that the conjecture records only the minimal missing ingredient; bracket closure of the concrete stabilizer is itself proved — \mathfrak{su}(3) = \ker(\mathrm{ev}_e) is closed under the commutator, hence a Lie subalgebra of \mathrm{Der}(\mathbb{O}) = \mathfrak{g}_2, since [D_1,D_2]\,e = D_1(D_2 e) - D_2(D_1 e) = 0 — so the strengthening is stateable whenever the conjectured \Phi materialises.

Two consequences are proved unconditionally. First, the dimension obstruction: a faithful linear action forces \dim \mathfrak{g} \leq (\dim V)^2. Second, its instantiation at the colour dimension: an 8-dimensional colour algebra admits no faithful action on a state space of dimension \leq 2, since 2^2 = 4 < 8 \leq 3^2 = 9 — so three strands are the minimal faithful colour host. The framework's three-strand baryon structure is thereby not an aesthetic choice but the smallest state space on which the octonionic colour symmetry could act at all; conversely, any proposed colour action on a smaller space is excluded by the cited rank invariant, not merely unlikely.

A calibration proved after the class was first stated sharpens where the open content lives. The abstract class quantifies over an arbitrary state space, and it is satisfied — tautologically — by the octonion base module itself: \mathfrak{su}(3) = \ker(\mathrm{ev}_e) is by construction a submodule of \mathrm{End}(\mathbb{O}), so the inclusion realises the faithful action on \mathbb{O} = \mathbb{C} \oplus \mathbb{C}^3, the \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathbf{3} colour decomposition of [dubois-violette-todorov2018]. The class therefore holds for \mathbb{O}, and that is exactly how far the tautology reaches. What remains conjectural — and is the intended content of the conjecture — is the action on the framework's own three-strand Hecke state space: an injective \Phi whose target is the braid-state module, compatible with its Hecke structure, not merely some faithful module somewhere.

What the class does and does not test. As formalised, the conjecture asks only for an injective linear map \mathfrak{g} \to \mathrm{End}(V), and that exists as soon as \dim \mathfrak{g} \le (\dim V)^2 (colourStabilizerAction_of_finrank_le); on the single-fibre three-strand space V^{\otimes 3} \cong \mathbb{Q}^8 it holds trivially, 8 \le 64, and says nothing about colour. The physically meaningful reading requires the action to commute with the braiding and with the fibre gauge algebra. That reading fails on the single-fibre space: at q = 1 the operators on (\mathbb{Q}^2)^{\otimes 3} commuting with the slot swaps and with \mathfrak{sl}_2 form a two-dimensional algebra (the decomposition V^{\otimes 3} = S^{(3)} \otimes V_{3/2} \oplus S^{(2,1)} \otimes V_{1/2} is multiplicity free), so no injective linear map from the eight-dimensional colour algebra lands there (no_colour_action_commuting_with_braiding_and_su2 in QOU/StandardModel/ColourOnSingleFibreThreeStrands.lean). Colour therefore needs structure beyond the single fibre, the same conclusion the N = 3 problem reaches for flavour.
rem:su5-hypercharge-n3-gate:
Remark \mathrm{SU}(5) is rung five of the level tower the fibre stands on. \mathrm{SU}(5) is not derived here, and nothing below should be read as deriving it. What the framework possesses is a family of levels among which \mathrm{SU}(5) is one, together with a proved statement about what occupying that level would force. It does not possess anything occupying it. The distinction is the whole content of this block.

The family is the Ocneanu parameter as a function of the Wenzl level,

  z_r \;=\; \frac{q^{r}}{[r]_q},
  \qquad [r]_q = \frac{q^{r} - q^{-r}}{q - q^{-1}},

whose r = 2 member is z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1) — the canonical trace parameter the framework actually runs on — and whose r = 5 member is z_5 \approx 0.32275 at the aether anchor. The Schur–Weyl row cap at level r is \ell(\lambda) \le r, so each level fixes an admissible row count: the framework sits at r = 2, the flavour fundamental would need r = 3, and \mathrm{SU}(5) is r = 5.

These levels are alternatives, not stages. The framework carries a single Markov trace parameter — production computes one z, the canonical z_2 = q^3/(q^2+1) — and the fibre-dimension result below fixes z from the fibre. So one fibre occupies one level; there is no sense in which the framework passes through r = 3 and r = 4 on its way to r = 5, and nothing is cumulative. Reaching a higher level means a different fibre, not a further step.

The level would fix the trace parameter, with nothing left to choose. This is the fibre-dimension result, proved for general N: a fibre of quantum dimension \dim_q V = [N]_q forces z\,[N]_q = q^N. So a genuinely five-dimensional fibre would carry z = z_5 as a consequence rather than as a fit, exactly as the two-dimensional fibre carries z_2.

That statement is a conditional, and its antecedent is not established. No construction in this framework produces a fibre of quantum dimension [5]_q, or of [3]_q; the theorem says what would follow if one existed, and restating its hypothesis as though it held would be the error the framework's own discipline names — a conditional lemma proves the implication, never the premise. What the corpus contains at r = 5 is a value of a rational function, not an object.

What is missing is therefore not the object but a construction supplying a different fibre. The framework has no construction yielding a fibre at any level other than r = 2. That is the same gap as the flavour problem, at a larger level: the three-dimensional fundamental would be r = 3, and no object of the single-fibre category can supply it, since every object of that category passing the \mathrm{Sym}^2 gate has even dimension. Climbing cannot be done from inside the fibre; it requires structure at the groupoid level, which is exactly what the truncation conjecture records as unavailable.

\mathrm{SU}(5) therefore sits strictly downstream of an already-open gate, and is further from reach than the flavour \mathrm{SU}(3) the framework has been unable to construct. It offers no route around that gate, since it presupposes it.

What the grand-unified organisation contributes anyway

One observation survives independently of whether any other level is ever reached, and it re-scopes the framework's open list.

In the Georgi–Glashow organisation one generation and its antiparticles occupy the exterior algebra \Lambda \mathbb{C}^5, with the five basis vectors labelled u, d, r, g, b [baez-huerta2010], so that \mathbb{C}^5 \cong \mathbb{C}^2 \oplus \mathbb{C}^3 — isospin and colour. There, hypercharge is not an additional datum; it is forced. The elements of \mathrm{SU}(5) commuting with all of \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathrm{SU}(3) are scalar on each block, \mathrm{diag}(\alpha,\alpha,\beta,\beta,\beta), and the determinant condition \alpha^2\beta^3 = 1 cuts \mathrm{U}(1) \times \mathrm{U}(1) down to one \mathrm{U}(1), generated by \mathrm{diag}(\alpha^{3},\alpha^{3},\alpha^{-2},\alpha^{-2},\alpha^{-2}). The grading of \Lambda\mathbb{C}^5 then fixes every hypercharge in the generation.

The framework records the missing hypercharge and the missing three-dimensional fundamental as two separate gaps — the first asking for a second crossing invariant independent of the writhe, the second for a three-dimensional object. Read through the 2 \oplus 3 block structure they are one gap: supply the colour triple and the determinant condition delivers \mathrm{U}(1)_Y with nothing further to choose; withhold it and Y stays underdetermined however much framing data is added. On this reading, searching for an independent second invariant may be the wrong shape of question.

What this does not establish. That the level-5 fibre's five dimensions would split as 2 \oplus 3 in the Standard-Model way is not shown here and is not a consequence of the tower — the tower fixes a row cap and a trace parameter, not a flavour–colour decomposition. Treating the two fives as the same five is the open question, not a result. Georgi–Glashow \mathrm{SU}(5) is in any case excluded by experiment on its proton-decay rate [baez-huerta2010]; what is at issue is the algebraic organisation, not the physical theory.
prop:neutral-lepton-fixes-charges:
Proposition One neutral lepton fixes every first-generation charge. Proposition. Let 5 = C \oplus V with C a colour triple (indices 0,1,2) and V an isospin doublet (indices 3,4), and let Q(\alpha) = T_3 + \alpha\,Y_0 with Y_0 = \mathrm{diag}(-2,-2,-2,3,3) the generator of the traceless commutant of \mathfrak{sl}_3 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2. On the matter content \bar 5 \oplus \Lambda^2 5:

  1. the doublet of \bar 5 has a member of charge 0 if and only if \alpha = \pm\tfrac16;
  2. this holds if and only if \mathrm{Tr}_{\bar 5 \oplus 10}(T_3^2) / \mathrm{Tr}_{\bar 5 \oplus 10}(Q^2) = \tfrac38;
  3. at \alpha = \tfrac16 the charges are (\tfrac13,\tfrac13,\tfrac13,-1,0) on \bar 5, and on \Lambda^2 5 they are -\tfrac23 on colour–colour wedges, +\tfrac23 and -\tfrac13 on colour–isospin wedges, and +1 on the isospin wedge;
  4. Q(-\alpha) is -Q(\alpha) with the two isospin indices exchanged, so the root \alpha = -\tfrac16 is the charge conjugate of the same table.

At either root every colour-singlet charge is an integer and every coloured charge of 5 is \mp\tfrac13.

Proof. The weights of Q(\alpha) on 5 are (-2\alpha,-2\alpha,-2\alpha,\tfrac12+3\alpha,-\tfrac12+3\alpha). The doublet of \bar 5 carries their negatives at indices 3 and 4, which vanish exactly at \alpha = -\tfrac16 and \alpha = \tfrac16. The trace ratio equals 1/(1+60\alpha^2), which is \tfrac38 exactly when \alpha^2 = \tfrac1{36}. The table in item 3 is the substitution \alpha = \tfrac16, with the charge of the wedge e_i \wedge e_j equal to the sum of the charges of e_i and e_j. Item 4 is a comparison of the five weights. \square

The table in item 3 is the charge assignment of d^c (three colours), e and \nu on \bar 5, and of u^c, u, d and e^c on \Lambda^2 5. The quark charges +\tfrac23 and -\tfrac13 are therefore consequences of one neutral lepton. They are no longer inputs.

Scope. The proposition has two inputs. The first is the matter content \bar 5 \oplus \Lambda^2 5, which is the Georgi–Glashow assignment as presented by Baez and Huerta [baez-huerta2010]. The framework does not derive it (the rung-five remark). The second is that one lepton has charge 0. This datum is a vanishing, not a measured value. The summands C and V are built objects in this corpus: C is the octonionic colour triple and V is the fibre of the quantum observable universe. Neither needs the flavour fundamental or the rung-five fibre, because the triple in 5 is colour.
prop:fermi-pair-wedge:
Proposition Fermi exchange puts a strand pair in the exterior square. Proposition. Let 5 = C \oplus V as in the neutral-lepton proposition, and call a two-strand state f : \{0,\dots,4\}^2 \to \mathbb{Q} a Fermi state if f(j,i) = -f(i,j).

  1. A Fermi state vanishes on equal labels and is determined by its values on i < j, so the Fermi states are indexed by the ten wedges e_i \wedge e_j.
  2. The ten wedges split by label type as 3 + 6 + 1: colour–colour, colour–isospin and isospin–isospin. There is no colour sextet, and exactly one colour singlet.
  3. At \alpha = \tfrac16 the excluded symmetric pair e_3 \otimes e_3 is a colour singlet of charge 2; the one colour singlet of the Fermi channel, e_3 \wedge e_4, has charge 1.
  4. The cubic trace of Y_0 is -30 on \bar 5, 30 on \Lambda^2 5, 30 on 5 and 270 on \mathrm{Sym}^2 5. Hence a copies of \bar 5 and c copies of \Lambda^2 5 have vanishing cubic trace if and only if a = c.

Proof. Item 1: f(i,i) = -f(i,i), and f(j,i) = -f(i,j) recovers the values with i > j. Items 2 to 4 are finite computations over the weights Y_0 = \mathrm{diag}(-2,-2,-2,3,3) and Q(\tfrac16). \square

Scope. Three inputs remain. Fermi exchange on strand pairs is assumed, as in the colour selection rule. That a multiplet is one strand or one strand pair is assumed. Vanishing of the cubic trace is imposed as a consistency condition, and it does not exclude vector-like content, since 5 \oplus \bar 5 also cancels. What this proposition removes from the matter-content input is the choice of \Lambda^2 over \mathrm{Sym}^2 for a strand pair, and the relative multiplicity of \bar 5 and \Lambda^2 5.
prop:strand-slot-separates-gen1:
Proposition The strand slot separates the first-generation quark states. Proposition. Place each first-generation quark state in one of four slots on 5 = C \oplus V: a single colour strand in \bar 5, or a strand pair of type colour\wedge e_3, colour\wedge e_4 or colour\wedgecolour in \Lambda^2 5, by the Georgi–Glashow assignment u_L, \bar u_L \mapsto colour\wedge e_3, d_L, \bar d_L \mapsto colour\wedge e_4, u_R, \bar u_R \mapsto colour\wedgecolour, d_R, \bar d_R \mapsto colour. Mark the states \bar u_L, \bar d_L, u_R, d_R as dual, meaning they sit in 5 \oplus \Lambda^2 \bar 5.

  1. Slot and dual flag together separate all eight states; the slot alone does not.
  2. The dual flag is set exactly when the chirality bit and the particle bit differ.
  3. At \alpha = \tfrac16 the slot charges are \tfrac13, \tfrac23, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac23, independent of the colour strand. Negated on dual states, they give +\tfrac23 on u, -\tfrac13 on d, and the negatives on \bar u, \bar d.

Proof. Items 1 and 2 are a case check over the eight states. Item 3 is the neutral-lepton proposition at \alpha = \tfrac16. \square

Scope. The chirality analysis in ChiralityIndependentOfCrossing shows the crossing sign cannot separate the sector and leaves one further label open. This proposition takes that label to be the strand slot. The slot assignment is the Georgi–Glashow embedding and is an input; so are the matter content, one neutral lepton and Fermi exchange, through the Fermi pair proposition.
rem:cal2-higgs-knot-coupling:
Remark The muon-ratio aether proxy as a Higgs-knot volume coupling. The canonical particle–knot table assigns the figure-eight knot 4_1 to the Higgs boson — an assignment with structural content of its own, since 4_1 is amphichiral, matching a scalar that is its own antiparticle. Read against that table, the muon-to-electron aether relation

  \frac{\mathfrak{m}_\mu}{\mathfrak{m}_e} \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(4_1)}{\hbar_q^2}

acquires a sharp interpretation: the muon's mass is the electron scale dressed by the Higgs knot's hyperbolic volume. What the Standard Model phrases as "the muon acquires mass through its Yukawa coupling to the Higgs field" the framework phrases as "the muon's mass proxy evaluates the volume of the Higgs knot" — the same structural role, played by \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \approx 2.0299 rather than a fitted Yukawa constant.

Two boundaries delimit this reading. First, it is interpretive: the identity is the weak-modulus aether calibration proxy, established independently of the table, and nothing new is derived by the relabelling. Second, the muon's identity knot remains the cinquefoil 5_1; the figure-eight enters the mass formula as the coupling object, not as the muon itself — the same division of roles the nucleon chain exhibits, where the mass-bearing volume (\mathcal{B}_3) is not the identity knot of any single constituent.
rem:a5-orbital-degeneracy-fracture:
Remark Orbital degeneracies fracture along A_5 irreducibles. If the archimedean truncation of the truncation conjecture is the right picture — observable-scale symmetry descending from the fibre's discrete automorphisms rather than a continuous rotation group — then atomic orbital degeneracies inherit a specific discrete fingerprint. Restricting the (2l+1)-dimensional \mathrm{SO}(3) representations to the icosahedral group A_5 \subset S_5 (the orientation-preserving automorphisms of the Bring fibre) gives, by exact character arithmetic:

orbital 2l+1 A_5 decomposition
s 1 \mathbf{1}
p 3 \mathbf{3}
d 5 \mathbf{5}
f 7 \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4}
g 9 \mathbf{4} \oplus \mathbf{5}
h 11 \mathbf{3} \oplus \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{5}

The s, p, d degeneracies are native — they are exactly the dimensions 1, 3, 5 of A_5 irreducibles and restrict irreducibly. Every degeneracy above five fractures: the group has no irreducible of dimension greater than 5, so the f orbital's seven states are, under the truncated symmetry, a composite of a \mathbf{3}' and a \mathbf{4} that a continuous rotation group would hold together. The branching arithmetic is standard finite-group representation theory, computed exactly.

The physical reading — that f-shell degeneracy is only approximate, with a fine-structure split along the \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4} seam — is conditional on the truncation conjecture and is recorded here as an interpretive consequence, not a prediction wired to any computation.

No falsifiability claim is made. One might argue that a truncated discrete symmetry cannot hold seven states exactly degenerate, while exact \mathrm{SO}(3) can, so the two pictures differ "at some resolution" on lanthanide-scale spectroscopy. Two objections. First, free-atom f-shell structure is already described to spectroscopic precision by rotationally invariant theory: states are labelled by J with (2J+1) degeneracy exact by isotropy, and the observed lifting is spin--orbit, in a J pattern rather than along a \mathbf{3}' \oplus \mathbf{4} seam. Second, and more fundamental, "at some resolution" names no resolution. The statement is compatible with every null result, which makes it untestable rather than falsifiable.

What is missing sits upstream of any bound. The branching establishes that the seam exists; it fixes no splitting magnitude, and none follows from character arithmetic alone. The experiment that would constrain such a splitting is itself undetermined, because the framework does not say how the icosahedral frame attaches to space:

  • if the A_5 frame is fixed in space, the atomic Hamiltonian is anisotropic, so the binding constraint is the Hughes--Drever family of clock-comparison tests of rotational invariance, which are far tighter than any lanthanide measurement;
  • if each atom carries an independently oriented frame, the anisotropy averages out and the constraint is line structure in an ensemble spectrum, which is the lanthanide measurement.

Until that is specified one cannot choose the experiment, let alone compute a bound. Supplying it is the open item here, ahead of any spectroscopic campaign.

This is a scope-(a) objection. The branching arithmetic stands: the six rows above were re-derived independently by \mathrm{SO}(3) \downarrow A_5 character arithmetic and reproduce exactly. Nothing here excludes the truncation picture. What is withdrawn is the claim that this block's value lies in falsifiability.
prose:sm-params-intro:
The 26 parameters of the Standard Model.

A derivation of the Standard Model must ultimately account for its free parameters. In the counting used here, the renormalisable Standard Model carries 19 parameters — 9 charged-fermion masses, 4 quark-mixing (CKM) parameters, 3 gauge couplings, 2 Higgs-sector parameters, and the strong-CP angle — and the neutrino-sector extension adds 7 more (3 masses, 3 mixing angles, 1 Dirac CP phase), for a total of 26. If the neutrinos are Majorana, two further phases appear; they are noted in the neutrino section and not counted in the 26.

The following sections walk the 26 parameters in chunks, one section per chunk, and record for each parameter its status in the framework using the tiers of the appendix introduction: input (one of the three calibration observables, not a prediction), proxy (a calibration proxy, exact by construction under the canonical pin), partial (a derived or conditional structure exists but the parameter is not closed), conjectural (a precise identification exists without derivation), and open (nothing here closes the parameter).

The headline count is stated up front so that the chunk tables cannot be misread as progress claims: of the 26 parameters, 1 is an input (m_e, the dimensional unit), 1 is a calibration proxy (m_\mu, pinning the aether modulus through the \beta-sector bar-skew calibration), 1 is partial (\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}, conditional structure with open per-loop measure), 2 are conjectural (\sin^2\theta_W, m_H), and 21 are open. No parameter beyond the calibration set is currently derived to experimental precision.
prose:sm-params-lepton-masses:
Charged-lepton masses (3).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_e input — the dimensional unit calibration triple
m_\mu proxy for the \beta-sector bar-skew calibration; as a proton-pinned prediction it misses the per-observable target by 970.2\times m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2
m_\tau open — no knot identification; the direct volume reading is refuted over a 25-knot search tau knot prediction

The electron mass is the framework's dimensional unit and is an input, not a prediction. The muon mass is the numerical proxy for the neutron \beta-sector bar-skew calibration P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta}: the ratio m_\mu/m_e \approx \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2 pins the aether modulus q_0, so under the canonical (muon) pin the muon mass is exact by construction — a calibration tautology, not an accuracy result. Under the experimental (proton) pin, m_\mu becomes a genuine prediction and misses its hundredfold-experimental-precision target by 970.2\times (211.2 ppb against a target of 0.2177 ppb), the \mu–p aether tension recorded in the precision-goals ledger. Either way, m_\mu does not count as a derived Standard-Model parameter.

The tau mass is open, and the obvious route has a recorded negative: the tau knot-prediction remark reports that a direct search over 25 hyperbolic knots found no K_\tau with m_\tau/m_e \approx \mathrm{Vol}(K_\tau)/\hbar_q^{k_\tau} within one percent — a scope-limited refutation of the naive volume reading as tested, not an exclusion of a tau carrier altogether. The framework does treat the tau's decay structure through the T(3,5) weak vertex — the tau leptonic-universality proposition derives lepton universality of the leptonic branching ratios from the Hecke amplitude's independence of the daughter lepton — but universality of ratios is not a mass. The missing object is the tau's carrier identification, together with whatever correction to the direct volume reading the 25-knot negative is pointing at.
prose:sm-params-quark-masses:
Quark masses (6).

Parameter Framework status
m_u, m_d open — quarks are composite constituents, not independent inputs
m_s, m_c open
m_b, m_t open

All six quark masses are open, and the framework's structural position makes the question different in kind from the Standard Model's. In the Standard Model the quark masses are six independent Yukawa couplings; in the framework, light quarks are not elementary inputs but components of composite braids — the up and down quarks appear as constituent structure of the Borromean baryon braid, with the proton–neutron split carried by an isospin assignment layer rather than by two independent masses. A constituent-level density (the structural identity relating the constituent density to the three-strand Markov trace) exists at the baryon level, but no construction extracts individual current-quark masses m_u, \ldots, m_t from it, and the heavy flavours are untouched here: no knot or braid identification exists for s, c, b, or t as mass carriers.

In sum: the framework currently predicts baryon-level masses and proposes to treat quark masses as derived constituent data, but the derivation of any individual quark mass — light or heavy — is open, and it is not yet established that the six current-quark masses are even the natural parameters of the framework's flavour sector.

This suggests the correct target is operational rather than definitional. Experimentally, no quark mass is measured directly: light-quark masses are scheme-dependent parameters extracted by inverting hadron spectroscopy through lattice computation and chiral perturbation theory, heavy-quark masses come from quarkonium spectra, and only the top — which decays before hadronizing — is reconstructed from decay products. The framework therefore need not define m_q at all; it need only derive the observables that the extraction procedures consume, and may then run the equivalent extraction to produce scheme-comparable numbers. Two consequences fix the programme. First, the cleanest extractable quantity is the isospin-breaking difference m_d - m_u: its experimental source is the neutron–proton splitting \Delta_{pn} after removing the electromagnetic self-energy, and the framework derives both \Delta_{pn} and its own electromagnetic–strong decomposition (the antisymmetric Coulomb crossing term of the Coulomb charge), so an extraction of "m_d - m_u in the framework scheme" is well-posed with no new inputs. Second, the combination m_u + m_d is not honestly extractable this way: its experimental source is m_\pi^2, and the charged-pion mass m_{\pi^\pm} is a physical calibration input — so any extraction through it would be circular. The parameters this section tabulates are thus reinterpreted: not six numbers the framework owes, but six scheme quantities of the observer's inversion procedure, of which the framework can currently ground one difference and must remain silent on the calibration-tainted combinations.
prose:sm-params-ckm:
Quark mixing (4).

Parameter Framework status
\theta_{12} (Cabibbo) open
\theta_{23}, \theta_{13} open
\delta_{\mathrm{CKM}} open — CP violation surveyed observationally only

All four CKM parameters are open. This paper records the experimental evidence for CP violation and the role of the complex phase \delta_{\mathrm{CKM}} in the observations chapter, and a spectral-form section discusses where a CP-violating phase could live in the categorical structure; but no categorical object has been constructed whose matrix elements yield a mixing matrix, no Cabibbo angle is derived, and there is no candidate mechanism relating the three mixing angles to braid or knot data.

The structural prerequisite is visible from the flavour discussion in the quark-mass section: a mixing matrix presupposes a flavour basis, and the framework has not yet fixed what its flavour degrees of freedom are beyond the isospin doublet. Until the flavour sector is defined categorically, the CKM parameters are not merely uncomputed — they are unposed.
prose:sm-params-gauge-couplings:
Gauge couplings (3).

Parameter Framework status Anchor
\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}} partial — conditional fixed-point structure; per-loop measure open EM-coupling fixed point, Habiro bar-involution
\sin^2\theta_W conjectural Weinberg angle, categorical
